summary: This bill prohibits the United States from providing any assessed or voluntary contributions to the World Health Organization.

scores.thoughts: The bill explicitly prohibits all assessed and voluntary US contributions to the WHO. This directly cuts a category of federal spending, aligning with reduced government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, or revenue collection.
While the WHO engages in global health work, the bill addresses only US funding to the organization and does not alter US domestic healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration, borders, visas, or refugee policy.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affect military or defense budgets or policy.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or related standards.
No provisions affect domestic welfare programs, entitlements, or safety-net spending.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policy.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
By cutting federal outlays, the bill produces a minor reduction in spending that could marginally aid debt reduction efforts, but the legislation is not framed around debt policy.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
The bill directly and completely prohibits US assessed and voluntary contributions to the WHO, which constitutes a clear reduction in this form of foreign aid/international organizational funding.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address labor rights, union power, or workplace regulations.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination policy.
